# Real-network frequency study

<!-- generated by tools/frequency/run.mjs from reports/raw/frequency.json; do not edit -->

How often each XDR union arm, and each shape behind the corpus entries and the reproduced bugs, occurs in real `LedgerCloseMeta`. Every number below is a count over the ledgers listed in the sample table, measured by `node tools/frequency/run.mjs`; nothing is extrapolated. Rates are transactions containing the shape per million transactions in that sample (all transactions in `tx_processing`, failed ones included).

## Full arm counts

Per-sample counts for every union arm and enum value seen, with first-seen ledger and up to three example transactions, are in `reports/raw/frequency.json` (`samples[].arms`, `samples[].shapes`).

## Method and limits

- Each ledger is decoded once by the reference implementation and walked by the same schema walker that produces `reports/coverage.md` (`tools/xdr-walk.mjs`), so arm names and the 376-arm universe are identical. Envelope and result subtrees are attributed to their transaction; header, upgrade and SCP arms count ledgers only.
- Shapes that are not a single union arm (muxed-ID ranges, P signers, auth-tree depth, map-key collisions, pool issuer order, SAC `trust()`, classic-op events) are detected in `tools/frequency/shapes.mjs`; each detector's rule is in that file.
- `sac.invoke_trust_fn` matches any contract function named `trust`; it does not confirm the contract is a Stellar Asset Contract. `sac.trust_creates_trustline` additionally requires a trustline `created` change in the same transaction.
- `sac.invoke_trust_fn` and `sac.trust_creates_trustline (#731 exact)` look only at the top-level `invoke_contract` function name, so they undercount. All 7 `soroban.creates_trustline` transactions on pubnet call SAC `trust()` as a sub-invocation in the authorization tree (under `batch`, `swap_split` or `swap_bridge`), so the #731 shape itself occurred 7 times in the pubnet sample. Each was checked by hand and replayed through wallet-backend: see `reports/replay-mainnet.md`.
- `pubnet-spread` is a systematic sample (every 100,000th ledger window), not a random one; `pubnet-recent` is one contiguous window. Rates describe these ledgers; they are not network-wide estimates.
- Corpus entries are testnet ledgers except the `mainnet-*` entries, which are mainnet transactions this study found; mainnet is on Protocol 29 in this sample, so Protocol 30 arms (CAP-84, CAP-88) can only appear on testnet.
